trust_decision.summary: httpd decides where one request field line ends and the next begins. A line that starts with SP/HTAB (obs-fold) is accepted as a new header because http_request:key_value left-strips the field name, so httpd and a front end can disagree on headers such as Transfer-Encoding. The decision is made in httpd_request:parse_headers.

landing_point.why: The summary names httpd header continuation. The parse_headers clause that splits field lines on CRLF is the obvious place, and the fix inserts its clause right there.

fix_sites.entry_point: Any HTTP/1.x request to an inets httpd server: header section parsed by httpd_request:parse_headers through the httpd_request_handler socket loop

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/inets/src/http_lib/http_chunk.erl:280-286 (chunked-trailer field-line parser in the shared http_lib package; the published fix did not touch it, so it is listed in O8)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The trailer parser is shared http_lib code that the client also uses (lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_handler.erl:958), and the client deliberately accepts and unfolds obs-fold (lib/inets/src/http_lib/http_response.erl:36, lib/inets/test/httpc_SUITE.erl:1401-1406). A solver can argue that trailers are a separate chunked-encoding feature, outside httpd request headers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The body and any pipelined next request share the binary that parse_headers walks. A body that contains CRLF+SP, or a value with internal SP/HTAB or OWS, must still be accepted, and so must bare-LF line endings (RFC2616 19.3 tolerance). Client-side obs-fold unfolding in the shared http_lib must keep working.

O6_input_shapes: bare LF followed by SP/HTAB (normalised to CRLF by lib/inets/src/http_server/httpd_request.erl:252-256 before the new clause)
fold split across TCP reads (CRLF at buffer end is continued by lib/inets/src/http_server/httpd_request.erl:248-251 and re-parsed)

O7_producer.where: lib/inets/src/http_lib/http_request.erl:35 (key_value strips leading whitespace from the field name, so a whitespace-led line becomes a valid header)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Whitespace-preceded first field line right after the request line: parse_version consumes the CRLF, so parse_headers starts on SP/HTAB with no CRLF prefix and the new clause never matches; key_value then left-strips the name.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: RFC 9112 treats this as a separate rule (whitespace between start-line and first field, section 2.2) rather than obs-fold (section 5.2), and the report shows only a fold after an existing header.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different function (parse_version -> parse_headers fallthrough at lib/inets/src/http_server/httpd_request.erl:284-287); cause in lib/inets/src/http_lib/http_request.erl:35

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Chunked request trailers: decode_trailer splits on CRLF with no SP/HTAB check, and the trailer lines are merged into the request header record through http_request:headers -> key_value (left-strip).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Trailers are a different chunked-encoding feature in shared http_lib that the client also uses, and the client intentionally tolerates obs-fold.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other package (http_lib vs http_server); reached from lib/inets/src/http_server/httpd_request_handler.erl:509-516 via lib/inets/src/http_lib/http_chunk.erl:105-106

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A tolerant 'unfold continuation' branch in key_value that joins a whitespace-led line onto the previous value only on one code path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: http_response.erl already unfolds obs-fold for the client (lib/inets/src/http_lib/http_response.erl:36), so a maintainer could plausibly mirror it for requests.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An extra LF-normalisation clause that rewrites a lone-LF+SP sequence to a form the new obs-fold clause does not match.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The parser already has several hand-written RFC2616 19.3 bare-LF rewrite clauses whose order decides which clause sees the bytes.

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / header parser differential (CWE-444), obs-fold and whitespace-led field lines

O10_build.toolchain: Erlang/OTP source build (autoconf, make, C compiler for erts); inets is pure Erlang
O10_build.project_tests: lib/inets/test/httpd_SUITE.erl (http_get group: missing_CR, max_header, ignore_invalid_header near lib/inets/test/httpd_SUITE.erl:172-175), lib/inets/test/httpc_SUITE.erl:1401 headers_with_obs_fold; run with common_test (ts/ct_run) on loopback sockets

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a CRLF+SP/HTAB -> 400 clause in httpd_request:parse_headers only, leaving the first-line case and chunked trailers open; or reject leading whitespace in shared http_request:key_value and break client unfolding.

out_of_scope_notes: The httpc response parser (lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_response.erl:336-340) accepts obs-fold by design and unfolds it in http_response; that is a client trust boundary, not httpd.

Chunked trailers can override content-length and other request headers through http_chunk:handle_headers (lib/inets/src/http_lib/http_chunk.erl:105-114); this is a separate trailer-merging issue, not pursued.
